issues.t: Transfer case oil leak can lock the wheels (recall)
issues.sym: Gear oil drips from the middle of the car near the transmission, a burning-oil smell, or whining from the drivetrain. In the worst cases owners report the wheels locking up at speed.
issues.why: The all-wheel-drive transfer case can leak its oil. Once it runs low, the bearings overheat and the drivetrain can seize. Mitsubishi recall 02V143 covers inspection, resealing and refilling, or replacement if the case is damaged.
issues.next: Look under the car for fresh gear oil. If you see a leak or hear grinding or whining from the middle of the car, don't drive it; have it towed. Ask a Mitsubishi dealer to check the VIN for recall 02V143 and to check the oil level even if the recall was done.

issues.t: Transfer case or output shaft failure
issues.sym: A loud bang under hard acceleration, then the car still moves but slips or flares when you give it a lot of throttle. You may also hear grinding from the middle of the car.
issues.why: The splines on the shaft that sends power from the transmission into the transfer case wear and can strip or break. Power then goes only to the front wheels and the center coupling can overheat. Towing the car with only two wheels on the ground can also ruin the coupling.
issues.next: Stop driving it hard and have it towed or driven gently to a shop that knows these all-wheel-drive cars. Only tow it on a flatbed with all four wheels off the ground.

issues.t: 6-speed manual grinding, jumping gears or failing
issues.sym: Grinding when shifting into first, second or third, the shifter landing in the wrong gear, or the transmission locking in one gear. Some owners report a sudden failure at highway speed.
issues.why: The synchronizer rings in the Getrag 6-speed wear, and owners report the gearbox failing at moderate mileage. Parts are scarce, so many cars need a rebuilt or used transmission.
issues.next: If it grinds, shift gently and get it checked soon. If it jumps out of gear or locks up, pull over safely and have it towed. Ask a transmission shop that knows the 3000GT for a quote before replacing it.

issues.t: Timing belt breaks or slips
issues.sym: The engine suddenly quits while driving and cranks but won't start, or you hear slapping or ticking from the front of the engine.
issues.why: The timing belt and its tensioner wear out and need replacing about every 60,000 miles. A tired tensioner lets the belt slip, and a broken belt can bend valves and cause serious engine damage.
issues.next: If you don't have proof the belt was replaced in the last 60,000 miles, have it done now along with the tensioner, idler and water pump. If the engine has quit, don't keep cranking it; tow it to a shop.

issues.t: Front seat belts won't retract
issues.sym: The driver or passenger belt stays slack, doesn't wind back in when you let go, or has to be fed back by hand.
issues.why: The front belt retractors wear out over time. Many owners have reported this to NHTSA across these model years, and a slack belt may not hold you well in a crash.
issues.next: Keep the belt snug by hand for now and get the retractor replaced soon. A slack seat belt is a safety problem, not just an annoyance.

issues.t: Engine knock from a spun bearing
issues.sym: A deep knock from the engine that gets louder with speed, often with low oil pressure or the oil light flickering.
issues.why: A connecting rod or main bearing has worn through. On these cars it is often linked to a dented oil pan from using it as a jacking point, or to running low on oil.
issues.next: Stop driving and shut the engine off. Check the oil level and have a shop listen to it. Driving with a knock can wreck the engine completely.

issues.t: Turbo oil seals leak and smoke
issues.sym: Blue-gray smoke from the exhaust, oil in the intake pipes or intercooler hoses, rising oil use, or a whine or rattle from a turbo.
issues.why: The two turbochargers wear inside with age. Worn seals let oil into the intake and exhaust, and noisy bearings mean a turbo is close to failing.
issues.next: Check the oil level often. Have a shop check for oil in the intake pipes and listen to the turbos. Replace failing turbos before they shed parts into the engine.

issues.t: Lifter tick
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping from the top of the engine, mostly right after a cold start.
issues.why: The hydraulic valve lifters wear and lose oil pressure. Owners say it is nearly unavoidable on these engines as they age, and one owner reports the tick lasting even after new lifters.
issues.next: Check the oil level and make sure you use the right oil. A light tick that fades as it warms is usually not urgent. Loud constant ticking should be checked by a shop.

issues.t: Oil leak from the valve covers
issues.sym: Oil on the top or sides of the engine, a burning-oil smell after driving, or a few drops under the car.
issues.why: The valve cover gaskets and seals harden with age and seep oil. Owners also report seepage around the oil filler cap.
issues.next: Have the leak source confirmed. New gaskets are a modest job, and fixing it keeps oil off hot exhaust parts.

issues.t: Chrome wheels peel and tires lose air
issues.sym: Tires keep going low or flat, and the chrome on the wheels flakes or peels, often on the inside of the rim.
issues.why: The factory chrome wheels corrode under the plating. The rough surface stops the tire bead from sealing, so air leaks out slowly.
issues.next: Check tire pressure weekly. A tire shop can clean and seal the bead area for a short-term fix, but badly corroded wheels need replacing.

issues.t: Automatic transmission shifts late or slips
issues.sym: Shifts from second to third or third to fourth come late, especially once the car is fully warm, or the engine revs flare between gears.
issues.why: The automatic transmission wears inside with age, and fluid that hasn't been changed makes it worse. Mitsubishi released an improved internal clutch for this transmission.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. A fluid service may help if it is just old fluid. If it slips or won't shift, get a transmission diagnosis before it fails completely.

issues.t: Clutch slipping or dragging
issues.sym: The engine revs rise without the car speeding up, the clutch engages near the top of the pedal, or it is hard to get into gear with the pedal down.
issues.why: The clutch disc wears out, and the hydraulic system that works it can leak or need bleeding. Hard launches wear it faster.
issues.next: Have the clutch fluid and hydraulics checked first. A slipping clutch will only get worse; plan a replacement before it leaves you stuck.

issues.t: Power steering leaks
issues.sym: Power steering fluid dripping near the front wheels, a whine when turning, or the steering getting heavier.
issues.why: The steering rack seals and the high-pressure hose wear and leak. Mitsubishi released a new power steering hose for these cars.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and keep it topped off. Have the leak traced; a hose is a much smaller fix than a rack.

issues.t: Rear-wheel steering fluid leak
issues.sym: Fluid drips near the rear of the car or the rear steering boots look swollen with fluid.
issues.why: VR-4 models steer the rear wheels slightly at speed. Its rack and linkages can leak as they age.
issues.next: Have a shop that knows the VR-4 find the leak. Replacing worn linkages is often enough.

issues.t: Long cranking, stumbling and stalling when cold
issues.sym: The engine takes a long time to start cold, hesitates or sags while warming up, or stalls.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued a service bulletin for long cold-start times, sagging during warm-up and stalling on these cars.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a shop to check the bulletin. Also check the idle control and fuel system before replacing big parts.

issues.t: Fuel starvation from a clogged in-tank filter
issues.sym: The engine stumbles, loses power or cuts out under hard acceleration or at high speed, then recovers.
issues.why: The filter on the fuel pump inside the tank can clog and starve the engine of fuel.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested under load. Replacing the pump and in-tank filter is the usual fix.

issues.t: Fuel smell from a leaking fuel sender
issues.sym: A gasoline smell in or around the car, especially after filling up, or a wet spot near the top of the tank.
issues.why: The fuel line connection at the sending unit on top of the tank can be bent or loosened, letting fuel seep out.
issues.next: Don't ignore a fuel smell. Avoid filling the tank to the top and have the sender area checked soon.

issues.t: Engine computer fails from leaking capacitors
issues.sym: The car is hard to start now and then, stutters or runs poorly, or the digital climate control display goes dark.
issues.why: Small capacitors inside the engine computer and climate control panel leak with age and corrode the circuit board. It is most common on early 3000GTs but can happen on later ones.
issues.next: Have a shop check the computer for leaking capacitors. Many owners send the unit out to be recapped instead of buying a new one.

issues.t: Water leaks into the cabin
issues.sym: Wet carpet, a damp smell, or water inside after rain or a car wash, often near the rear hatch, doors or roof.
issues.why: Seals around the rear hatch, door glass and roof harden and let water in. Mitsubishi also published a water-leak test for the Spyder's retractable top.
issues.next: Find where the water gets in with a hose test. Dry the carpet fully to prevent mold and rust.

issues.t: Shaking when braking or brakes pulling
issues.sym: The steering wheel or car shakes when you brake, or the car pulls to one side under braking.
issues.why: Warped or worn rotors cause shaking. A sticking caliper causes pulling. The rear rotors also hold the parking brake and are hidden behind covers, so rust builds up unseen.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected soon, especially if the car pulls. Rotors and pads, or a caliper, are the usual fix.

issues.t: Power window grinds or drops
issues.sym: The window moves slowly, grinds or clicks, goes crooked, or drops into the door.
issues.why: The window regulators wear out and break on these cars.
issues.next: Avoid using the window until it is fixed, and cover the opening if it won't close. A new regulator or motor is the usual repair.

issues.t: Active exhaust valve stuck
issues.sym: The exhaust sound no longer changes as it should, or there is a rattle from the rear of the exhaust.
issues.why: VR-4 models have a valve in the exhaust that changes the sound. It seizes from corrosion.
issues.next: It doesn't harm the engine. Many owners replace the rear exhaust section instead of freeing the valve.

issues.t: Bouncy ride or pulling from worn struts
issues.sym: The car bounces after bumps, feels floaty, clunks, or pulls to one side on a flat road.
issues.why: Struts, strut mounts and bushings wear out on high-mileage cars.
issues.next: Have the suspension and alignment checked. Worn struts are replaced in pairs.
